kind: v36 ladder: the attack is RUN per pool per cell; endpoints are counted, not reconstructed

production_evaluation.statement: success = P(target covered) x P(pipeline verifies | covered) = (2N/r) x 0.987779 = 2^-138.22. The binding term is COVERAGE 2N/r = 2^-138.21, not the width: a pool of N records reaches at most a 2N/r fraction of the exponent space, and r=2^255 against N=2^115.65 leaves 139 bits unreachable. The v35 0.396243 is WITHDRAWN: it was a 12-20-bit key-hit rate presented as a 168-bit success probability.

protocol: pool = one challenge c, nb bases, ONE shared walk list of length ell (true Cartesian product, every (i,l) record built as a real EC point); target planted inside the pool so coverage is 1 and the measured quantity is the key-filter x recovery success; success requires the binding relation and the lift to verify [s]P0 == T

rungs_below_floor.disclosure: no rung is reported as clearing the floor unless its CP lower endpoint does; the v35 'two of five' accounting came from reconstructed endpoints and is withdrawn

width_effect.measured: success q = 1.0 at all four widths 12/16/20/24 in every split (300/300 pools)
width_effect.reading: width does NOT move success: a covered target shares its record's full x coordinate, so the truncated filter fires at every width. The truncation therefore costs WORK (a 2^-b coincidence buys a lift that fails) and buys no success. The v35 package read a 12-20-bit hit rate as the success of a 168-bit key; that transfer is refuted by these cells.

uncovered_control.statement: an uncovered target still produces truncated hits at these widths, and EVERY one of them fails the full-point check: 165 hits, 0 false accepts. A filter coincidence never manufactures a secret.
